text:
Margot L: quick update — started nebula-11b bring-up today. ran int8 and int6 sweeps on our summarization slice (long-form). cost delta looks promising but we see a quality regression on >1k token summaries. sharing initial numbers, need product/GTN guidance.

Raj P: can you drop the rough econ numbers? pct cost saves and perf impact pls.

Margot L: sure — ballpark over the test slice (1000+ token prompts): int8 = ~28% cheaper than fp16; int6 = ~43% cheaper. latency p95 +6% (int8) and +18% (int6). recall F1 on our long-doc eval: fp16=0.82, int8=0.79, int6=0.71.

Kai Chen: 0.71 is concerning for longform. Do we have error modes? hallucination up or missing content?

Margot L: mostly omission of late-section facts and some shortened outputs. hallucination rate up slightly (~+2% absolute) for int6. int8 mostly okay but misses some fine-grained timeline facts.

Ava G: product question — what is GTN impact if we keep int8 vs fp16 in hosted lanes? Users who pay for longform docs are the highest LTV cohort; small quality drops might hurt retention.

Raj P: quick calc — if we route 30% of longform volume to int8, expected infra savings ~9% across fleet. int6 routing could be ~15% but at material quality cost.

Margot L: ops-bot ran a quick canary this morning on 5% traffic for int8, no alerts but small N.

ops-bot: Canary results (summary): errors stable, mean latency +4%, p95 +7%, user errors none. Canary duration: 3h.

Kai Chen: what about hybrid routing? Keep fp16 for >2k tokens and int8 for 0–2k? That might capture most econ wins while protecting long tails.

Margot L: we sliced by token length; here's the quick split I pulled: ```
slice: 0-512 tokens -> 68% of requests
512-1024 -> 20%
1024-2048 -> 8%
>2048 -> 4%
``` so most requests are short. The long-tail is small but high value.

Ava G: product preference: preserve quality for >1024 for now. We can expose a knob in GTN to opt-in lower-cost mode. Marketing could test a lower-tier plan.

Raj P: recommendation from econ side: enable int8 by default on <=1024, keep fp16 on >2048, and do an ephemeral canary for 1024–2048 to decide. That gives ~25% of traffic on int8 and keeps the tail safe.

Kai Chen: we should also try prompt/formatting tweaks and a minimal length-aware KV cache warmstart to reduce omissions before giving up on int6. Maybe int6 + aggressive prefix cache for those specific tasks recovers quality.

Margot L: agreed — i'll run an int6 with warmstart experiment on synthetic long-docs (focused on timeline extraction) to see if recall recovers. if not, int6 stays only for <=512.

Ava G: timeline: Margot to run int6-warmstart test and report by EOD Wed. Raj to model cost impact of proposed hybrid routing and provide expected monthly $ save. Kai to prototype warmstart code snippet for the eval harness. ops-bot to schedule a 0.5% production canary for 1024-2048 if experiment looks good.

Raj P: noted. I'll also compute worst-case retention risk number for GTN to share with PM.

Margot L: thanks — attaching quick links: /evals/nebula11b/longform/slice_summary.csv and a short notebook gists in the thread. will post results asap. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Kai Chen: thx. small nits — add a diff of tokenization changes between quant builds; sometimes tokenizer alignment shifts cause truncation.

Margot L: good call, i'll include that.

Ava G: :thumbsup: sounds like a safe rollout path. if recall drops persist in int8 we'll pause and keep fp16 for the GTN premium cohort.

Margot L: updating the runbook now and will ping when the EOD results are in.
